Standard: Store payloads maintain the minimum fuze arm delay required to meet all safe escape criteria. Store minimum arm time (or distance) after release does not fall within the minimum fuze arm time required to maintain safe escape criteria (or is otherwise considered an early burst). Any potential for early burst does not result in fragmentation to the launch air vehicle that exceeds a 1 in 10,000 threshold for overall Ph (the product of the Ph given a premature detonation and the probability of a premature detonation). Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examine design documentation for safe and arming devices (e.g., fuze) to determine minimum arm time, to include any failure modes and demonstrated reliability of safe and arming devices and fuzes. This may be determined by service specific munitions safety review boards. Analysis.
  (1) Conduct SEA by modeling the air vehicle, weapon, and fragment trajectories that include the point of detonation. Early burst analysis assumes that the weapon detonates at the minimum fuze arm time and subsequent distance from the launch platform along a weapon flight trajectory. Probability of hit by fragmentation to the air vehicle is modeled considering factors such as the air vehicle release conditions and flight path, the weapon’s trajectory and orientation after launch, and the warhead’s fragmentation data informed by static arena testing, and if applicable, fuze reliability data, specifically fuze failure rate.
  (2) Evaluate the minimum safe arming distance or fuze arm time setting that is possible once the munition has left the air vehicle. If applicable for the analysis, including fuze reliability (failure rate), as well as if potential munition failure modes should be considered. Determine the probability that a warhead fragment could impact the delivery air vehicle in the event of an early burst.
  (3) Determine if evaluated probability meets the minimum threshold for escape criteria, 1 in 10,000. The probability of a single fragment hit to the delivery air vehicle may not exceed the established Ph and Ph/EB risk criteria for early burst. Determine if there is protection to prevent critical damage to the air vehicle from the munition fragmentation if early detonation should occur.
  (4) Identify the set of flight conditions (altitude, speed, and engagement range) that will provide the air vehicle protection from the munition detonation given fuze failure. This set of flight conditions, at a minimum, should include the planned flight test and release points as part of the live fire testing. Ideally, the available data should characterize the entire employment envelope, weapon flight modes, and fuze arm times.
  (5) In cases where the Ph does not meet minimum safe escape criteria, determining Pk of the launch air vehicle may be conducted and correlated to the damage tolerance of the air vehicle to show compliance (or inform an overall risk). Probability of kill is determined through modeling the vulnerable areas of the launch air vehicle obtained from vulnerability analyses. Test.
    (1) Ground test: Conduct static arena test with production representative warhead to characterize the warhead fragmentation pattern, fragment size, fragment travel velocity, and fragment travel distance. Static arena test data will inform the SEA.
    (2) Flight test: Instrumented live fire flight testing may be conducted to verify weapon flyout behavior, validate weapon flyout models, and measure fuze arm time prior to testing with a live AUR. Live fire flight testing may inform distance at early burst or assess safe and arm device reliability in order to update early burst probability assessment. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Examination.
(2) Verify that the safe release envelope necessary to maintain safe escape for store employment is defined and is accessible to flight crew (e.g., safe escape tables in weapon delivery procedures, safe escape tools in mission planning).
